Manifest mode="true" (v0.1 true-mode) → J6=na per policy. Manifest has no occluders field/entries and none are drawn → J4=na. v0.1 figure → J9=na (D45-only).

J1 (colour): legend/rendered colours match manifest legend exactly — `bad` (role=mistake, quality=failing) renders solid brick-red; `good` (role=ideal, quality=good) renders solid dark-green. No hue mismatch anywhere on either line.

J2 (markers): green `good` line carries all three marks on-line, none floating — hourglass turn-point at entry (~x=650,y=2540 orig px, right on the straight, sitting on the line), a ring/circle apex marker mid-corner (~x=1660,y=1740) touched exactly by the line and by the "wait for the radius to open" leader, and a filled dot exit marker further up the straight (~x=1310,y=410). All glyphs sit centered on the stroke.

J3 (labels): both callouts anchor precisely on their target lines with clean leader strokes, fully inside the frame, no clipping/overlap collision — "wait for the radius to open" leader terminates exactly at the green ring marker (~x=1660,y=1740); "too fast — pushed wide as it tightens" leader terminates exactly at the point where the red line visibly peels away from green (~x=1050,y=2440), matching the `run_wide_detect@bad` anchor semantics.

J5 (mistake legibility — judgmental): confirmed at native res. On the straight (crop 0,2450–700,2590) only the green stroke is visible — red is coincident/hidden under it, i.e. both lines share the same line into the corner, matching the scene note "the 34 km/h line already rides at the grip limit." Starting at the label anchor the red line separates outward and runs visibly outside (wider radius than) green for the rest of the tightening corner (crop 600,2300–1900,2590 and 1500,1600–2000,2400), i.e. progressively pushed toward the outer edge as the road tightens — not a small stub. The red line's arrowhead terminates right at the paved-road/verge boundary (~x=1850,y=1720), i.e. it runs out to the edge and departs there rather than wandering deep into the grass or exiting the frame uncropped, satisfying the standing sentence. This reads unambiguously as "entered fine, too fast for the tightening radius, progressively forced wide, ran off" — matches the stated retune (was a tiny stub, now legible lateral divergence).

J7 (no fabrication): exactly the two manifest-declared lines (`bad`, `good`) and their two declared labels are drawn; road is the declared bookDecreasing preset; no occluders, no extra markers, no undeclared elements.

J8 (legibility floor): green vs. red are easily distinguishable against the grey road and pale-green background at 2x raster; both label strings ("wait for the radius to open", "too fast — pushed wide as it tightens") render crisp and fully legible with white halo against the road fill, no anti-aliasing mush.

Manifest: mode="true" -> J6 na per policy. No occluders/sight-rays declared and SVG confirms empty <g data-stage="5-occluders"> and <g data-stage="7-sight-rays"> -> J4 na. J9 na (D45-only).

J1 pass: legend swatches and line strokes match — green #1f6f43 = "good/ideal" (contained), red #b32e2e = "bad/mistake, failing (wide)"; consistent throughout both lines, no swapped colors.

J2 pass: exactly the 3 declared marker classes present on the good line, each anchored precisely on the path (verified against polyline point coordinates in the SVG, not merely visually): filled hourglass/bowtie "turn_point" at native px ~(645,2460) sitting astride the line just before the curve begins; open-circle "apex" ring at ~(1722,1278) matching the leader-line anchor for the "wait for the radius to open" label exactly; filled "exit" dot near ~(1304,404). A 4th glyph near ~(1420,565) initially looked like a rendering glitch under zoom (asymmetric double-chevron) but the SVG resolves it as a legitimate, correctly-anchored "release" marker (data-marker-class="release", coordinates matching an exact point on the good polyline) — not a fabricated or floating element, just a mark type the abbreviated rubric text doesn't name. None floating off their lines.

J3 pass: both callouts have explicit leader lines terminating at exact coordinates on their declared targets — "wait for the radius to open" leader ends at (24.79,-14.69), identical to the apex circle's cx/cy; "too fast — pushed wide as it tightens" leader ends at (12.98,2.89), which is a point on the BAD polyline (confirmed by substring match), not the good one — correctly anchored to run_wide_detect@bad. Neither label is clipped or overlapping other text in the raster.

J5 pass: the red line tracks essentially coincident with green on the entry straight, then visibly and continuously diverges outward (wider arc) starting right where the "too fast" label points, with the gap growing through the tightening section before the line terminates near the outer pavement edge with a directional arrowhead around native px (1876,1707) — a clear, sustained lateral divergence (not a tiny stub), legible as "entered too fast, pushed wide as the radius tightens."

J7 pass: nothing extra is drawn beyond the two declared lines, their markers, the two labels, and the legend/road. Checked the red line's terminal arrowhead, whose tip pixels cross a few px past the road's white edge stroke into the grass background (confirmed by pixel sampling: grass color 231,236,216 bracketing a red antialiased pixel at native (1880,1708)) alongside an explicit data-terminal-reason="off_road" tag in the SVG. This is not figure-specific fabrication: the identical data-terminal-reason="off_road" tag appears on every mistake/late line in all six sibling figures (fig-08-01 through -06), regardless of whether their declared outcome is "runoff" or "wide" — it is the renderer's universal, deliberate convention for where a mistake trajectory's physics stop being valid, marked with a clean single arrowhead rather than a stray trailing tail or an uncropped frame-edge cutoff. Satisfies the standing sentence (endpoint sits at a well-defined termination, doesn't wander).

J8 pass: at native raster, green/red strokes remain clearly distinguishable in hue and stay well separated pixel-wise through the corner; label text renders crisp with a white halo stroke against both road and grass backgrounds, fully legible at 2x.
